concept.body: Solving a right triangle with geometric means: label the two hypotenuse segments p and q and the whole hypotenuse (p + q). ALTITUDE = √(p·q). Each LEG = √(hypotenuse · its adjacent segment). Match the relationship to what you're solving for, and cross-check with a² + b² = c².

explanationVariants: The altitude is the geometric mean of the two segments.

widget.prompt: The hypotenuse segments are 4 and 9. Find the altitude.

commonErrors.feedback: 6.5 = (4 + 9)/2 is the average. The altitude is √(4 × 9) = 6.
13 = 4 + 9 is the whole hypotenuse. The altitude is √(4 × 9) = 6.

steps.body: With the geometric-mean toolkit you can solve a right triangle from surprisingly little. Given the two hypotenuse segments, the altitude and both legs all follow. The trick is choosing the RIGHT relationship: altitude from the two segments, each leg from the hypotenuse and its adjacent segment.

widget.prompt: This hypotenuse is 15. Slide the foot until the two segments read 3 and 12, and take the altitude from the readout rather than from a formula.
widget.successFeedback: 3 and 12, altitude 6 — since 6² = 36 = 3 × 12. The status line is also reporting the other two means: each leg squared equals the whole hypotenuse times that leg's own segment, 15 × 3 = 45 and 15 × 12 = 180. One figure, three geometric means, all holding at once.
widget.lowFeedback: p is under 3 — the foot is too far left and the altitude is still short. Slide right.
widget.highFeedback: p is over 3 now. Ease back left. Every position on the way obeys h² = p·q, so there is no risk of losing the relationship while you hunt for the right one.

predict.prompt: The two hypotenuse segments are 3 and 12. Before computing: the altitude will be…

options.label: 6 — the square root of the product

predict.reveal: 6. The altitude is the geometric mean, √(3 × 12) = √36, not the arithmetic mean 7.5. The two means agree only when the segments are equal, which is the one position where the foot sits at the midpoint.

explanationVariants: With segments 3 and 12, the whole hypotenuse is 15; the leg adjacent to 3 is √(15 × 3) = √45.

widget.prompt: Segments are 3 and 12 (hypotenuse 15). Which expression gives the leg adjacent to the segment of length 3?

options.feedback: leg = √(hypotenuse × adjacent segment) = √(15 × 3) = √45. That's the geometric-mean rule for a leg.
√(3 × 12) is the ALTITUDE (the two segments). A leg uses the whole hypotenuse × adjacent segment: √(15 × 3).
√(15 × 12) is the OTHER leg (adjacent to the 12 segment). The leg near 3 is √(15 × 3).
Subtraction isn't a geometric-mean relationship. The leg is √(15 × 3).

steps.body: Use the diagram's labels to choose the relationship: the two hypotenuse segments are 4 and 9, so the altitude is h = √(4·9) = 6. In general, the altitude uses the two segments; a leg uses the whole hypotenuse and the segment touching that leg. Label those roles before choosing a square root.

widget.prompt: You want the altitude of the right triangle. Which two lengths are the geometric mean built from?

options.label: the two hypotenuse segments
options.feedback: The altitude is the geometric mean of the two segments: h = √(p·q).

options.label: the whole hypotenuse and a leg
options.feedback: That mixes the relationships. The ALTITUDE uses the two SEGMENTS, not the hypotenuse and a leg.

options.label: the two legs
options.feedback: The legs aren't combined for the altitude. Use the two hypotenuse segments: √(p·q).

options.label: the hypotenuse and the altitude
options.feedback: That's circular — you're solving FOR the altitude. It comes from the two segments.

widget.prompt: The hypotenuse segments are 4 and 16. Find the altitude.

commonErrors.feedback: 10 = (4 + 16)/2 is the average. The altitude is √(4 × 16) = √64 = 8.
20 = 4 + 16 is the whole hypotenuse. The altitude is √(4 × 16) = 8.

steps.body: It all ties back to Pythagoras as a check. Once you have both legs and the hypotenuse, confirm a² + b² = c². The geometric-mean relationships and the Pythagorean theorem describe the same right triangle from two angles — they must always agree.

widget.prompt: A right triangle has legs 15 and 20. What is the hypotenuse? (√(15² + 20²))

commonErrors.feedback: 35 = 15 + 20 adds the legs directly — but the hypotenuse uses SQUARES: √(225 + 400) = √625 = 25.

hints: Segments are 9 and 16, so the hypotenuse is 25.
The leg adjacent to the segment 16 is √(hyp × 16) = √(25 × 16).
explanationVariants: The leg adjacent to the 16 segment is √(25 × 16) = √400 = 20.

widget.prompt: Hypotenuse segments are 9 and 16 (hypotenuse 25). Find the leg adjacent to the segment of length 16.

commonErrors.feedback: 12 = √(9 × 16) is the ALTITUDE, not this leg. The leg adjacent to 16 is √(25 × 16) = 20.
15 = √(25 × 9) is the leg adjacent to the OTHER segment (9). The one adjacent to 16 is √(25 × 16) = 20.

takeaways: Altitude from the two segments; each leg from the hypotenuse and its adjacent segment.
Sketch and label p, q, and the hypotenuse before choosing a relationship.
Cross-check the result with the Pythagorean theorem.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: put similarity to work in the real world — indirect measurement and scale.
